title: Retinal Vasoreactivity and Optical Coherence Tomography as Non-Invasive Markers for Cerebral Microangiopathy
summary:
This study examines possible correlations between retinal vasoreactivity and / or the thickness of certain retinal layers with the volume of cerebral white matter lesions.
If such a correlation could be found, the above mentioned parameters could serve as prognostic tools for the risk of the presence of white matter lesions, achieved with affordable means.

interventions.name:
75 patients, 50 to 80 years old, will be compared with ophthalmologically and vascular healthy control persons (n = 75, each group).

The retinal reactivity of both groups will be examined before and after hyperventilation. The retinal thickness will be determined in both groups, too using OCT.
